question: Are the schools near 116-02 Rockaway Beach Boulevard exposed to flooding?

plan.rationale: The query specifies a specific street address, indicating a locatable point near which schools are to be assessed for flood exposure.

claims.text: This address is mapped within the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) and is modeled to be inside FEMA flood zone X, per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970379F, effective 2007.
No Hurricane Ida high-water marks were surveyed within 800 meters of this address; the nearest USGS-surveyed mark is 11,126 meters away.

Experimental: satellite-detected surface water about 14 hours after Hurricane Ida showed no water polygons within 500 meters of this address; the nearest water polygon is 2,776.1 meters away and is primarily marsh, shoreline, and park water.

No FloodNet sensors are deployed within 600 meters of this address, and 36 NYC 311 flood-related complaints were filed within 200 meters in the last five years, with the most common descriptor being Sewer Backup (Use Comments).
The latest reading at Sandy Hook, NJ, shows a tide of 5.43 feet above mean lower low water, observed at 2026-09-26 17:36.

Within 800 meters of this address, there is 1 MTA subway entrance inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and another inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise). Within 1500 meters, there are 4 NYC DOE schools, all inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 3 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario.

Experimental: a TTM model forecasts a peak surge residual of 0.53 meters at The Battery about 9 hours ahead, and projects about 0.04 flood-related 311 complaints per week within 200 meters for the next 96 days.
